questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
Consider the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP) 3.0 (2026 to 2031, outlay about Rs 565.50 crore):
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme implemented by the Department of Land Resources.
2. It gives every land parcel a 14-digit Unique Land Parcel Identification Number (ULPIN), also called Bhu-Aadhaar.
3. It is implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
Which of the above are correct?
questions.why: DILRMP is run by the Department of Land Resources (Ministry of Rural Development), not the Housing Ministry. The new phase also plans paperless registration and upgrades 75 Sub-Registrar Offices.
questions.insight: Land is a State subject (List II), so States build the land records and the Centre funds and standardises them.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: In September 2026 a new Chairperson (Bhagwat Prasad Makwana) was appointed to the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis (NCSK). Which is correct about NCSK?
opts: It is a body under the Ministry of Labour and Employment
It is a non-statutory body under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, working through periodic Government resolutions
It is a constitutional body under Article 338
It is a statutory body created by the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
questions.why: NCSK was set up under the NCSK Act, 1993, but the Act lapsed on 29 February 2004. The Commission has continued since then through extended resolutions. The new appointments run to 31 March 2028.
questions.insight: Article 338 is for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes; NCSK looks into the welfare of sanitation workers and manual scavengers.

src.name: PIB, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Which is correct about the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY), which completed seven years in 2026?
opts: All farmers with any landholding get Rs 6,000 a year in three instalments
It is a free pension with no contribution from the farmer
It is open only to farmers above 60 years
Small and marginal farmers aged 18 to 40 contribute Rs 55 to Rs 200 a month and get a minimum pension of Rs 3,000 a month at 60
questions.why: PM-KMY is voluntary and contributory, with the Centre matching the farmer's contribution. Landholding must be up to 2 hectares. The spouse gets a family pension of Rs 1,500 a month.
questions.insight: Do not mix it up with PM-KISAN, which gives Rs 6,000 a year as income support.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The International Day of Democracy is observed every year on:
opts: 10 December, to mark the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
15 September, established by a UN General Assembly resolution of 2007
15 August, to mark independence from colonial rule
questions.why: The UN General Assembly passed the resolution in 2007, and the day was first observed in 2008.
questions.insight: In India, free and fair elections are part of the Constitution's basic structure.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Political parties in India are registered with the Election Commission under which provision, and donations above what amount in a year must be reported to the Commission?
opts: Article 324 of the Constitution; above Rs 2 lakh
Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951; above Rs 2,000
Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951; above Rs 20,000
questions.why: Registration is under Section 29A. A party must report contributions above Rs 20,000 from a donor in a year (Section 29C).
questions.insight: A registered party that is neither national nor State party is a Registered Unrecognised Political Party (RUPP).

src.name: Representation of the People Act, 1951 (India Code)

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: As per the three-language formula in the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020:
opts: Hindi is compulsory in all States
English must be one of the three languages in every school
No language is imposed on any State, but at least two of the three languages must be Indian languages
questions.why: NEP 2020 keeps the three-language formula but gives States, schools and students the choice. At least two languages must be Indian languages.
questions.insight: NEP 2020 also promotes teaching in the mother tongue or home language, at least up to Class 5.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Cabinet approved raising the EPFO wage ceiling for mandatory coverage in September 2026. The ceiling changed from:
questions.why: The ceiling rose from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 (Cabinet 16 September, effective 17 September). It is the first revision since 2014 and brings over 51 lakh more employees under mandatory coverage.
questions.insight: Total government support for the pension scheme (EPS) rises to about Rs 11,339 crore a year.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: India's real GDP growth for the first quarter (April to June) of 2026-27 was estimated at:
opts: 6.9%, the same as a year earlier
questions.why: Real GDP grew 7.8% (nominal 10.3%) and real GVA grew 8.2%, the highest Q1 growth of the last four years.
questions.insight: GDP is estimated by the National Statistics Office (NSO) under MoSPI.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: India's GDP series released in February 2026 uses which base year, replacing which earlier base?
questions.why: MoSPI released the new series with base year 2022-23 on 27 February 2026, replacing the 2011-12 series. An updated series was released on 31 August 2026 with new price indices.
questions.insight: A base year is the benchmark year used to measure real changes without the effect of inflation.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Japan Credit Rating Agency (JCR) upgraded India's long-term sovereign rating in September 2026. The new rating is:
opts: A+ with a positive outlook, up from A
BBB with a stable outlook, up from BBB-
AA- with a stable outlook, up from A-
A- with a stable outlook, up from BBB+
questions.why: JCR raised its rating one notch to A- and also raised India's country ceiling to A. It cited steady growth and a sounder financial system.
questions.insight: S&P (BBB) and Morningstar DBRS (BBB) raised India's rating in 2025 as well.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0 is operational until:
opts: 31 March 2027, with a cap of Rs 25,000 crore
31 March 2027, or until guarantees worth Rs 2.55 lakh crore are issued, whichever is earlier
31 March 2030, with no cap on guarantees
questions.why: The Cabinet approved ECLGS 5.0 on 5 May 2026. Scheduled passenger airlines get a 90% guarantee, with additional credit up to Rs 1,500 crore per borrower.
questions.insight: ECLGS is run through the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC) via lending institutions.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The RBI ran Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auctions in September 2026. VRRR is used to:
opts: Raise the cash reserve ratio automatically
Absorb excess liquidity from the banking system
questions.why: In a reverse repo the RBI borrows money from banks, taking surplus liquidity out of the system. In the VRRR the rate is set by auction, and the cut-off rate was 5.24% in September 2026.
questions.insight: The fixed-rate tools are the SDF (floor of the corridor) and the repo rate.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Districts as Export Hubs (DEH) initiative, led by DGFT, is best described as:
opts: A new scheme giving each district a fixed grant for exports
An initiative to set up special economic zones in every district
A WTO agreement on district-level trade
A convergence framework that draws on existing schemes, grown from One District One Product (ODOP)
questions.why: DEH makes each district a unit of export planning. District Export Promotion Committees prepare action plans and act as a forum for exporters' grievances.
questions.insight: DGFT works under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: In the World Economic Forum's Global Gender Gap Index 2026, India's rank and score were:
opts: 131st among 145 economies, with 64.5% of the gap closed
questions.why: India retained its 131st position with 64.5% parity. Iceland ranked first for the 17th year. The global gap is 69.2% closed.
questions.insight: The Index measures four areas: economic participation, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The 18th BRICS Summit was hosted by India in New Delhi on 12 and 13 September 2026 under the theme:
opts: Partnership for a Digital and Green Future
Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability
Strengthening Global South Cooperation for Inclusive and Sustainable Governance
questions.why: India holds the BRICS chair in 2026, and the summit adopted the New Delhi Declaration. India had earlier chaired BRICS in 2016 (Goa) and 2021 (virtual).
questions.insight: The previous summit's declaration (Rio de Janeiro, 2025) was titled on strengthening Global South cooperation.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The 26th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO), attended by India's Prime Minister, was held on 31 August and 1 September 2026 in:
questions.why: The summit adopted the Bishkek Declaration. India backed proposals including making English an official SCO language. The chair for 2026-27 passes to Pakistan.
questions.insight: India chaired the SCO in 2022-23 and hosted a virtual summit in 2023.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: In an award at the end of August 2026, the Court of Arbitration under the Permanent Court of Arbitration, in the Indus Waters Western Rivers case, held that:
opts: The Treaty stands terminated since April 2025
Water sharing under the Treaty has been suspended until a new agreement
Only the World Bank can decide Treaty disputes
The Indus Waters Treaty remains in force and cannot be placed in abeyance unilaterally
questions.why: The Court said the Treaty has not been terminated or suspended and that India's decision on abeyance is not permissible under the Treaty or international law.
questions.insight: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1960 between India and Pakistan, with the World Bank as a signatory. India placed it in abeyance in April 2025.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The 'Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026' became US law on 18 September 2026. Which is correct?
opts: It lifts sanctions on Russian energy exports
It applies only to Iranian oil and not to Russia
It lets the President impose tariffs, up to 100%, on goods from the top five importers of Russian oil or gas, and extends the Iran Sanctions Act to 2031
It bans all trade between the United States and India
questions.why: The Act was passed by the Senate 86-11 in August and became Public Law 119-111. The tariff power is discretionary, not automatic.
questions.insight: It matters to India because India buys Russian crude oil, though the sources do not name India directly.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The GSLV-F17 mission launched on 4 September 2026 from Sriharikota carried EOS-05, described by ISRO as:
opts: India's first satellite to orbit the Moon
A navigation satellite of the NavIC constellation
India's first imaging satellite from geosynchronous orbit
questions.why: GSLV-F17 was the 19th GSLV flight. After a series of orbit-raising burns, EOS-05 is to be placed in the geostationary orbit at 85.5 degrees East.
questions.insight: A geostationary satellite stays above one point of the equator because its orbit takes 24 hours.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026, notified in August 2026, are meant to:
opts: Move India to two time zones
Make GPS the only legal time source
Set one legal, traceable Indian Standard Time across the country, with CSIR-NPL as the scientific basis
questions.why: The Rules cover the generation, maintenance and spread of IST and take effect 180 days after publication. IST is distributed through regional laboratories and ISRO's NavIC.
questions.insight: CSIR-National Physical Laboratory in New Delhi maintains India's national time standard.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan Awards, held in September 2026 on Swachh Vayu Diwas, rank cities on:
opts: Actions taken under their clean air plans, not measured air quality
Their measured annual average PM2.5 levels
questions.why: The ranking is based on reported implementation of city action plans under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), not on pollution readings. Ward-level surveys covered over 7,400 wards.
questions.insight: 7 September is the International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The UN General Assembly adopted the 'Correct the Map' resolution on 4 September 2026 (164 in favour, 1 against). Which is correct?
opts: It is legally binding on all member states
It encourages the use of the Equal Earth and other equal-area maps; it is non-binding and was led by Togo and the African Union
It bans the Mercator projection in all UN publications
It changes the recognised borders of African countries
questions.why: The text asks governments, schools and companies to use equal-area maps when relative size matters. The EU said it has no bearing on borders or sovereignty.
questions.insight: The Mercator map stretches areas near the poles, which makes Africa look smaller than it is.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: In the Global Financial Centres Index 40 (September 2026), GIFT City ranked:
questions.why: GFCI 40 was published on 16 September 2026 and covers 117 centres in its main index.
questions.insight: GIFT City in Gujarat is India's first International Financial Services Centre, regulated by the IFSCA.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: India's nationwide HPV vaccination campaign, launched on 28 February 2026 from Ajmer, offers:
opts: A free single dose to 14-year-old girls at government facilities; over 80 lakh doses had been given by September 2026
A paid two-dose course to all women above 30
A free dose to all boys and girls at birth
questions.why: Uttar Pradesh recorded the highest number of vaccinations, with more than 22 lakh girls covered. HPV vaccination continues in routine immunisation after the campaign.
questions.insight: Human papillomavirus causes most cases of cervical cancer, so vaccination before exposure is the best prevention.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
Consider India's first soil carbon payments to farmers (September 2026):
1. They went to smallholders in Punjab and Haryana, with the first payments released at Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana.
2. They were made by the Grow Indigo programme with ICAR's technical guidance, with credits issued under the Verra VM0042 methodology.
3. They were paid from the Union Budget by the Ministry of Agriculture.
Which of the above are correct?
questions.why: The payments came from a private-led programme, not from the Union Budget. Farmers had adopted practices such as direct seeded rice, reduced tillage and crop residue management.
questions.insight: Soil carbon credits reward farming that stores more carbon in the soil or cuts emissions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nauru informed the United Nations in 2026 that it is now officially the Republic of Naoero. The country lies in:
opts: The south-western Pacific (Micronesia), about 40 km south of the Equator
The Indian Ocean, west of the Maldives
questions.why: Naoero is a raised coral island in Micronesia, about 1,300 km north-east of the Solomon Islands. It has no official capital; government offices are in Yaren.
questions.insight: Its old name Nauru is replaced in the UN list, and its international code changes from NRU to NRO.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Naoero (formerly Nauru) is described as:
opts: The world's smallest independent republic, covering about 21 sq km
The largest island nation in the Pacific
questions.why: With about 12,000 people on 21 sq km, it is the smallest republic and the third-smallest country after Vatican City and Monaco.
questions.insight: It has no rivers; its limited fresh water and phosphate mining shaped the island's economy and landscape.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following does NOT share a border with Kosovo?
questions.why: Kosovo is a landlocked country in the central Balkans, bordered by Serbia, North Macedonia, Albania and Montenegro. Its capital is Pristina.
questions.insight: Kosovo declared independence from Serbia on 17 February 2008. India does not recognise it as an independent country.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: China has approved a large hydropower project in the lower reaches of the Yarlung Tsangpo, and India has asked it to protect downstream interests. This river is known in India as the:
opts: Siang or Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh, later the Brahmaputra
questions.why: The Yarlung Tsangpo flows east across Tibet, turns sharply south and enters India in Arunachal Pradesh as the Siang. It becomes the Brahmaputra in Assam and the Jamuna in Bangladesh.
questions.insight: India is a lower riparian state, so upstream dams raise questions about flow data and downstream impact.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Yarlung Tsangpo makes a sharp U-turn, called the Great Bend, around which Himalayan peak?
questions.why: The river wraps around Namcha Barwa in south-eastern Tibet before flowing into India.
questions.insight: The Great Bend gorge is one of the deepest in the world, which is why it is considered for hydropower.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Lipulekh Pass, in the news for border trade and the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, lies in:
questions.why: Lipulekh is in Pithoragarh district, Uttarakhand. The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra has used this route since 1954, and Nepal claims the area.
questions.insight: Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura are the territory Nepal claims.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following mountain passes is correctly matched with its State or Union Territory?
questions.why: Nathu La is in Sikkim, Shipki La is in Himachal Pradesh, Bomdi La is in Arunachal Pradesh and Zoji La is in Ladakh/Jammu and Kashmir.
questions.insight: Border trade and Kailash Mansarovar Yatra batches have used Nathu La and Lipulekh.

src.name: MEA, Rajya Sabha reply on border trade

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Strait of Hormuz, where disruptions in 2026 have affected trade, links:
opts: The Black Sea and the Aegean Sea
The Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman
The Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden
The Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea
questions.why: The strait lies between Oman and Iran and is the only sea route from the Persian Gulf to the open ocean.
questions.insight: Because much of the world's oil passes through it, ports outside it, such as Sohar, gain importance.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Sohar Port, highlighted as a gateway that avoids the Strait of Hormuz under the India-Oman CEPA, is located on the:
opts: Gulf of Oman, outside the Strait of Hormuz
Persian Gulf, inside the Strait of Hormuz
questions.why: Sohar is on the Gulf of Oman in northern Oman, between Muscat and Dubai. It gives access to sea lanes without entering the Persian Gulf.
questions.insight: The India-Oman CEPA came into force on 1 June 2026.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of these countries does NOT border the Gulf of Oman?
questions.why: The Gulf of Oman is bordered by Oman, Iran, Pakistan and the United Arab Emirates.
questions.insight: It is the north-western arm of the Arabian Sea.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: NOAA kept an El Niño Advisory in September 2026 and said the event may become very strong. El Niño is:
opts: An unusual warming of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean
An unusual cooling of the central equatorial Pacific
A cyclone that forms over the Bay of Bengal
A warm current in the North Atlantic
questions.why: The warm phase of the El Niño Southern Oscillation weakens the trade winds and shifts rain away from the western Pacific.
questions.insight: The opposite, cooler phase is called La Niña.

src.name: NOAA Climate Prediction Center, ENSO Diagnostic Discussion

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: El Niño years are generally associated with which impact on the Indian southwest monsoon?
opts: An earlier withdrawal of the monsoon only
Weaker monsoon rainfall and a higher risk of drought
Heavier monsoon rainfall and floods every time
questions.why: El Niño often reduces monsoon rainfall over India, though a positive Indian Ocean Dipole can offset some of the effect.
questions.insight: The link is a tendency, not a rule: some El Niño years have normal rainfall.

src.name: NOAA Climate Prediction Center, ENSO Diagnostic Discussion

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Niño 3.4 region, used to monitor El Niño, lies in:
opts: The central equatorial Pacific, roughly 5°N to 5°S and 170°W to 120°W
The Indian Ocean off Sri Lanka
questions.why: The Niño 3.4 sea-surface temperature anomaly is the main index; NOAA reported it at about +2.1°C in October 2026.
questions.insight: An anomaly above +0.5°C for several months signals El Niño conditions.

src.name: NOAA Climate Prediction Center, ENSO Diagnostic Discussion

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: IMD recorded extremely heavy rain over Uttar Pradesh in late September 2026. In IMD's classification, 'extremely heavy' rainfall in 24 hours means:
opts: 204.5 mm or more (about 20 cm or more)
questions.why: IMD classes 64.5 to 115.5 mm as heavy, 115.6 to 204.4 mm as very heavy and 204.5 mm or more as extremely heavy.
questions.insight: Terai districts flood easily because the land is flat and rivers block drainage.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is correct about a Western Disturbance (WD)?
opts: It is a summer wind that blows from the Thar desert
It originates in the Pacific Ocean
It is an eastward-moving extratropical system that brings winter rain to north-west India, drawing moisture mainly from the Mediterranean
It is a tropical cyclone from the Bay of Bengal
questions.why: WDs travel on the subtropical westerly jet stream and bring rain and snow to the western Himalayas and the north-western plains.
questions.insight: When a WD meets a tropical system such as a depression, rain can become very heavy.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: In the IMD classification, a system with sustained winds of 28 to 33 knots is called a:
questions.why: A depression has winds of 17 to 27 knots, a deep depression 28 to 33 knots, a cyclonic storm 34 to 47 knots, and a severe cyclonic storm 48 to 63 knots.
questions.insight: IMD tracked a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal in late September 2026.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Terai region, which is prone to floods in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, is:
opts: A dry desert belt in Rajasthan
A coral reef region in the Bay of Bengal
A low-lying marshy belt south of the Bhabar, along the Himalayan foothills
A high plateau in central India
questions.why: Streams that sink in the porous Bhabar belt re-emerge in the Terai, making it damp and flat.
questions.insight: Flat terrain and a high water table make waterlogging common after heavy rain.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The UN resolution of 4 September 2026 encourages the use of the Equal Earth map. The Mercator projection, in contrast:
opts: Shows all areas in true proportion
Is a conical projection used for the tropics
Is the same as the Equal Earth projection
Preserves local shapes but exaggerates areas near the poles
questions.why: Mercator is a cylindrical, conformal projection: angles are preserved but areas near the poles are stretched, so Africa looks smaller than it is.
questions.insight: Equal Earth (2018) is an equal-area projection that keeps relative sizes correct.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: On a true-area basis, Africa is about how many times larger than Greenland, which looks similar in size on a Mercator map?
questions.why: Africa covers about 30.4 million sq km, while Greenland covers about 2.2 million sq km.
questions.insight: Mercator makes high-latitude landmasses look much larger.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Mayun (Perim) Island lies in which strait, linking the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden?
questions.why: Perim sits in the Bab-el-Mandeb strait between Yemen and Djibouti and belongs to Yemen. It guards a key route for Suez Canal traffic.
questions.insight: The Suez Canal joins the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Suez Canal links:
opts: The Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea
The Black Sea and the Caspian Sea
The Atlantic and the Pacific Oceans
The Baltic Sea and the North Sea
questions.why: It shortens the sea route between Europe and Asia, avoiding the long trip around Africa.
questions.insight: The Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The retreat (withdrawal) of the southwest monsoon from India normally begins from:
questions.why: The monsoon advances from the south-east and retreats from the north-west, with withdrawal usually starting in September.
questions.insight: Tamil Nadu receives its main rain from the retreating (north-east) monsoon from October.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Sone (Son) river, which joins the Ganga near Patna in Bihar, is a:
opts: A right-bank tributary of the Ganga
questions.why: The Son rises near Amarkantak and joins the Ganga near Patna, entering from the right (south) bank.
questions.insight: Left-bank tributaries of the Ganga include the Ghaghara, Gandak and Kosi.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The subtropical westerly jet stream, which carries Western Disturbances to India, is a:
opts: Wind that blows only in summer from the south-west
A cold air mass over the Arctic
Fast, narrow band of upper-air winds blowing west to east
questions.why: The jet stream is found in the upper troposphere. In winter it lies south of the Himalayas, steering disturbances towards north India.
questions.insight: In summer it shifts north of the Himalayas, which helps the monsoon set in.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A 'hanging glacier' is best described as:
opts: A glacier that has fully melted
A tributary glacier that ends abruptly above the main valley glacier or on a cliff
A glacier that flows into the sea
A glacier formed only in the Antarctic
questions.why: Hanging glaciers sit high on steep slopes, so ice can break off and fall, which is a hazard in the Himalayas.
questions.insight: Rapid warming can destabilise them and trigger avalanches and glacial floods.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: In the Himalayas, which belt of porous pebbly deposits lies at the foot of the Shiwaliks and absorbs the streams that come down?
questions.why: Streams sink into the coarse Bhabar and re-emerge in the Terai. Bhangar and Khadar are old and new alluvium of the plains.
questions.insight: Bhabar is not good for farming but is important for groundwater recharge.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: India submitted 'The Painted Haveli Towns of Shekhawati' to UNESCO on 1 June 2026. This places it on:
opts: The List of World Heritage in Danger
India's Tentative List for World Heritage nomination
The World Heritage List of inscribed sites
questions.why: A Tentative List is a country's inventory of sites it intends to nominate; being on it is a required step before a full nomination. The serial entry covers 14 towns in Jhunjhunu, Churu and Sikar in Rajasthan.
questions.insight: It was submitted under cultural criteria (iii), (iv) and (v).

src.name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Tentative Lists

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: The painted havelis of Shekhawati in Rajasthan are known for:
opts: Frescoes on the walls of merchants' mansions, built mainly from the mid-19th century to the 1930s
questions.why: Marwari merchants who earned wealth in colonial cities built richly painted havelis in their home towns such as Mandawa, Nawalgarh and Fatehpur.
questions.insight: The region is often called an open-air art gallery.

src.name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Tentative Lists

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: Which of the following is a criterion used by UNESCO to judge a cultural site such as the Shekhawati towns?
opts: A site must be more than 5,000 years old
Criterion (iv): an outstanding example of a type of building or architectural ensemble
Criterion (x): significant natural habitats for biodiversity
questions.why: Criteria (i) to (vi) are cultural and (vii) to (x) are natural. Shekhawati was proposed under (iii), (iv) and (v).
questions.insight: A site needs to show 'Outstanding Universal Value' to be inscribed.

src.name: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Tentative Lists

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: Hindi Diwas, observed on 14 September (with the 6th All India Official Language Conference in 2026), marks the day in 1949 when:
opts: The Eighth Schedule was added to the Constitution
Hindi became the national language by a court order
The Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi in the Devanagari script as the Union's official language
The Official Languages Act was passed by Parliament
questions.why: The Constituent Assembly adopted the decision on 14 September 1949. Article 343 declares Hindi in Devanagari as the Union's official language.
questions.insight: India has no 'national language' in the Constitution; Hindi is the official language of the Union.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution directs the Union to promote the spread of the Hindi language?
questions.why: Article 351 is a directive for the Union to promote Hindi. Article 343 deals with the official language itself and Article 348 with the language of the courts.
questions.insight: The Eighth Schedule lists 22 recognised languages.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: The Constituent Assembly's compromise on the official language, called the Munshi-Ayyangar formula, provided for:
opts: Hindi in Devanagari as the official language, with English continuing for 15 years
questions.why: The compromise settled a long debate between supporters of Hindi and those wanting English or regional languages to continue.
questions.insight: The Official Languages Act, 1963 later allowed English to continue even beyond 1965.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: The Cabinet Mission (1946) proposed which of the following?
opts: Direct election of the Constituent Assembly by all adults
A three-tier federation with provincial groups, instead of a separate Pakistan
questions.why: The Mission rejected the demand for a separate Pakistan. It proposed a weak Centre, provinces in Groups A, B and C, and a Constituent Assembly elected by provincial legislatures.
questions.insight: Its members were Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution:
opts: Lists the Union, State and Concurrent subjects
Gives the allocation of Rajya Sabha seats
Lists the tribal areas of the Northeast
Lists the languages recognised by the Constitution; it has 22 languages today
questions.why: Dogri, Bodo, Maithili and Santhali were added in 2003 by the 92nd Amendment.
questions.insight: Tulu is a major language that is not yet in the Eighth Schedule.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: The Tulu language is spoken mainly in:
opts: The Malabar coast of Tamil Nadu
Coastal Karnataka (Dakshina Kannada and Udupi) and northern Kerala (Kasaragod)
questions.why: Tulu is a Dravidian language with its own old script (Tigalari), and it has a long tradition of the Bhuta Kola ritual.
questions.insight: People have long demanded its inclusion in the Eighth Schedule.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: Dogri, whose traditional script is called Dogra Akkhar, was added to the Eighth Schedule by the:
questions.why: The 2003 amendment added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali. Dogri is spoken mainly in the Jammu region.
questions.insight: The 21st Amendment (1967) added Sindhi; the 71st (1992) added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: Rani Avantibai Lodhi, a heroine of the Revolt of 1857, was the queen of:
questions.why: She took charge of Ramgarh after her husband's ill health, rejected the British Court of Wards and led local rulers and peasants in 1857.
questions.insight: She defeated the British in the Battle of Kheri in November 1857 and died in March 1858 rather than surrender.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: The 'Court of Wards' policy, used against rulers such as Rani Avantibai's Ramgarh, meant that:
opts: The British paid a pension to the ruler
The British took over the administration of an estate whose ruler was seen as unfit or a minor
The ruler was made the head of a court
The estate was given to the Nizam
questions.why: It allowed the British to manage estates of minors or incapable rulers, and it often led to annexation or resentment.
questions.insight: The Doctrine of Lapse (Dalhousie) was a related annexation tool.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: Vinoba Bhave, whose birth anniversary falls on 11 September, started the Bhoodan Movement in 1951 at:
questions.why: Bhoodan asked landowners to donate land for the landless. Vinoba was chosen by Gandhi as the first individual satyagrahi in 1940.
questions.insight: He received the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 1958 and the Bharat Ratna in 1983.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: Vinoba Bhave's movement that followed Bhoodan, in which villages were given up for common ownership, was called:
questions.why: Gramdan villages were meant to hold land in common, and the Sarvodaya movement worked for the welfare of all.
questions.insight: Bhoodan began in 1951 and Gramdan became its main form from the late 1950s.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay, whose 150th birth anniversary falls in September 2026 (born 15 September 1876), is best known as a:
opts: Bengali novelist, author of Devdas and Parineeta
Hindi poet of the Chhayavad school
questions.why: He wrote Devdas (1917), Parineeta and Srikanta. His novel Pather Dabi was banned by the British government in 1927.
questions.insight: Pather Dabi is about a revolutionary secret society.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: E.V. Ramasamy (Periyar), born on 17 September 1879, founded the:
questions.why: He later led the Dravidar Kazhagam (1944). He took part in the Vaikom Satyagraha of 1924 against caste restrictions on temple roads.
questions.insight: His journal Kudi Arasu (1925) spread the movement's ideas.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: The Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25), in which Periyar took part, was a protest for:
opts: The right of lower castes to use roads near the Vaikom temple in Kerala
Wages of mill workers in Ahmedabad
questions.why: It was one of the first campaigns against untouchability and caste restrictions on public roads. Gandhi supported it.
questions.insight: The Temple Entry Proclamation in Travancore followed in 1936.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: Which party was formed in 1944 from the Justice Party under Periyar's leadership?
questions.why: The Justice Party, formed in 1916 to represent non-Brahmins in Madras Presidency, was renamed Dravidar Kazhagam in 1944.
questions.insight: Later, the DMK split off from it in 1949 under C.N. Annadurai.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: Bhagat Singh, born on 28 September 1907, was a leader of which revolutionary organisation formed in 1928?
questions.why: He worked with Chandrashekhar Azad and others. He and B.K. Dutt threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929.
questions.insight: He was executed on 23 March 1931, observed as Shaheed Diwas.

src.name: PIB, Prime Minister's tribute on Shaheed Diwas

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: 'Inquilab Zindabad', made popular by Bhagat Singh, was first raised by:
questions.why: The Urdu poet and freedom fighter Hasrat Mohani coined it in 1921. Bhagat Singh and his comrades used it widely.
questions.insight: Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt shouted it after the Assembly bomb on 8 April 1929.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: Bhagat Singh's Naujawan Bharat Sabha was formed in 1926 mainly in which city?
questions.why: It encouraged young people to join the freedom struggle with a socialist and secular outlook.
questions.insight: The Lahore Conspiracy Case trial followed the killing of the police officer Saunders in December 1928.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai (born 5 September 1872) started which swadeshi venture in 1906?
opts: The Tata Iron and Steel Company
The Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company, between Tuticorin and Colombo
questions.why: He challenged the British shipping monopoly and was called 'Kappalottiya Tamizhan' (the Tamil helmsman).
questions.insight: He was jailed in 1908 for sedition after supporting a strike in Tuticorin.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: 'Vande Mataram', whose 150 years of composition are being commemorated, was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in:
opts: 1875, and later included in his novel Anandamath
questions.why: It was first sung at the Congress session in 1896 by Rabindranath Tagore and was adopted as the national song on 24 January 1950.
questions.insight: The Government is holding a year-long commemoration.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: The Dadasaheb Phalke Award, given at the National Film Awards (the 72nd were presented on 22 September 2026), is:
opts: India's highest award in cinema, first given in 1969
questions.why: The 2024 Dadasaheb Phalke Award went to actor Anant Nag. The first recipient in 1969 was Devika Rani.
questions.insight: The awards are run by the Directorate of Film Festivals under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: Kathakali, a classical dance-drama, belongs to which State?
questions.why: Kathakali tells stories from the epics through elaborate makeup, costumes and hand gestures (mudras), with music and drums.
questions.insight: Odissi is from Odisha, Manipuri from Manipur and Kuchipudi from Andhra Pradesh.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: Which of the following was a major port of ancient India for trade with the Roman world, on the Malabar coast?
questions.why: Muziris (near Kodungallur, Kerala) traded spices and pepper for Roman gold. The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea describes the trade.
questions.insight: Lothal was a Harappan dockyard in Gujarat, and Tamralipti was a port on the Bengal coast.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: The Harappan dockyard at Lothal, a sign of India's ancient maritime trade, is in:
questions.why: Lothal is near the Gulf of Khambhat in Gujarat, and had a dockyard and warehouses.
questions.insight: Harappans traded with Mesopotamia through the Persian Gulf.

questions.subject: History & Culture
questions.q: The 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea' is:
opts: A Buddhist text from Sri Lanka
A first-century CE Greek guide to sea trade routes, ports and goods of the Red Sea, Arabia and India
questions.why: It lists ports and trade goods, including those of the Indian coasts.
questions.insight: It is a key source for Indo-Roman trade.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched on 30 August 2026. Which is correct?
opts: It is a radio telescope placed on the far side of the Moon
It launched on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy from Kennedy Space Center and is heading to the Sun-Earth L2 point
It launched on an ISRO GSLV from Sriharikota to orbit the Moon
It was placed in low Earth orbit by the Space Shuttle
questions.why: Roman flew from Launch Complex 39A in Florida and is travelling to an orbit around the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point, about 1.5 million km from Earth.
questions.insight: NASA said first images are expected by early 2027.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The Sun-Earth L2 point, where the Roman telescope is headed, is:
opts: On the surface of the Moon
In low Earth orbit at 400 km
About 1.5 million km from Earth, on the side away from the Sun
Between the Earth and the Sun, about 1.5 million km from Earth
questions.why: At L2 the Sun, Earth and Moon are all on the same side, which makes shielding and cooling easier for infrared telescopes.
questions.insight: The James Webb Space Telescope is also at L2, and India's Aditya-L1 is at the Sun-Earth L1 point.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is mainly designed to:
opts: Study dark energy, find exoplanets and survey the sky in infrared over a wide field
Detect gravitational waves from the ground
questions.why: It has a mirror about the same size as Hubble's but a much wider field of view.
questions.insight: It is named after NASA's first Chief of Astronomy, Nancy Grace Roman, called the 'Mother of Hubble'.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: Aditya-L1, India's solar mission, is placed near which point?
questions.why: L1 lies between the Sun and Earth about 1.5 million km from Earth, and gives an uninterrupted view of the Sun.
questions.insight: L2, on the far side, suits deep-space telescopes.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: DRDO signed its first high-value deep-tech agreement under the Technology Development Fund (TDF) in September 2026. The project is to develop:
opts: An indigenous 20 mK dilution refrigerator for quantum applications
questions.why: It was signed with a start-up, Zero mK India Pvt Ltd (Alwar, Rajasthan), under the Rs 500 crore deep-tech corpus.
questions.insight: TDF is a Ministry of Defence programme run by DRDO to involve start-ups, MSMEs and industry.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: A dilution refrigerator is needed for quantum computers because:
opts: It cools the room for engineers
It stores the data of the computer
It supplies electricity to the processors
Qubits need extremely low temperatures, close to absolute zero, to keep their quantum states
questions.why: Heat disturbs fragile quantum states, so superconducting qubits are kept at millikelvin temperatures.
questions.insight: Absolute zero is 0 K, which is -273.15 degrees Celsius.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: A temperature of 20 millikelvin is closest to:
questions.why: 20 mK is 0.02 K above absolute zero (-273.15 degrees Celsius), so it is about -273.13 degrees Celsius.
questions.insight: Kelvin has no negative values; zero kelvin is absolute zero.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The National Quantum Mission, approved by the Cabinet in April 2023, has an outlay of about:
opts: Rs 6,003.65 crore for 2023-24 to 2030-31, run by the Department of Science and Technology
questions.why: It supports four Thematic Hubs: IISc Bengaluru (computing), IIT Madras with C-DoT (communication), IIT Bombay (sensing and metrology) and IIT Delhi (materials and devices).
questions.insight: The goal is to build intermediate-scale quantum computers with 50 to 1,000 physical qubits.

src.name: DST, Cabinet approves National Quantum Mission

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is considered secure because:
opts: Any attempt to eavesdrop disturbs the quantum states and can be detected
It sends data faster than light
It needs no key at all
questions.why: QKD uses quantum properties of light particles to share a secret key, and spying alters the signal.
questions.insight: India's National Quantum Mission includes quantum communication as one of its four verticals.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The Government approved the Biovigilance Programme of India in 2026. It is meant to:
opts: Monitor adverse events linked to organ and tissue transplantation, led by the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission
Certify the safety of genetically modified crops
questions.why: It joins the Pharmacovigilance Programme (medicines) and the Materiovigilance Programme (medical devices) to widen India's patient-safety net.
questions.insight: The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission, at Ghaziabad, publishes the Indian Pharmacopoeia.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: Pharmacovigilance is the science of:
opts: Detecting and preventing adverse effects of medicines
questions.why: The Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (PvPI), coordinated by the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission, records adverse drug reactions.
questions.insight: Materiovigilance does the same for medical devices.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam, built by BHAVINI, attained first criticality on 6 April 2026. A fast breeder reactor:
opts: Uses thorium as the primary fuel from the start
Produces more fissile material than it consumes, using plutonium and a fertile blanket
Uses only natural uranium and heavy water
questions.why: PFBR is the second stage of India's three-stage programme. Its blanket is designed to hold thorium-232, which turns into uranium-233.
questions.insight: Kalpakkam is in Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: In India's three-stage nuclear power programme, the third stage is meant to use:
opts: Natural uranium in pressurised heavy water reactors
Light water reactors with enriched uranium only
questions.why: Stage one uses PHWRs on natural uranium, stage two uses fast breeders to make plutonium and U-233, and stage three uses thorium-U-233 cycles.
questions.insight: India has large thorium reserves in monazite sands.

src.name: PIB, Nuclear Energy Technology in India

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: Thorium-232 itself is not fissile. It becomes useful as fuel because it is:
opts: Fertile: when it absorbs a neutron it changes into fissile uranium-233
questions.why: Fertile materials breed new fuel, while fissile materials such as U-233, U-235 and Pu-239 sustain the chain reaction.
questions.insight: India follows a closed fuel cycle, reprocessing spent fuel to reuse materials.

src.name: PIB, Nuclear Energy Technology in India

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: National Space Day is observed on 23 August because on that day in 2023:
opts: Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon's south pole, making India the fourth country to land on the Moon
India launched its first satellite, Aryabhata
The Mangalyaan mission entered Mars orbit
questions.why: The 3rd National Space Day in 2026 was held at Ahmedabad with the theme 'Towards Viksit Bharat: Innovating, Collaborating and Aspiring to Global Space Leadership'.
questions.insight: India was the first country to land near the lunar south pole.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The landing spot of Chandrayaan-3's Vikram lander on the Moon was named:
questions.why: The name was announced on 26 August 2023. The Chandrayaan-2 impact site is called Tiranga Point.
questions.insight: The Pragyan rover explored the area around Shiv Shakti Point.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: India's GSLV, used for the EOS-05 launch on 4 September 2026, differs from the PSLV in that it:
opts: Uses an indigenous cryogenic upper stage to put heavier satellites in higher orbits
Uses only solid fuel in all stages
Can launch only from outside India
questions.why: GSLV is a three-stage vehicle with a cryogenic third stage, suited to geosynchronous transfer orbits.
questions.insight: PSLV is mainly used for polar and sun-synchronous orbits.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: NavIC, whose signals help distribute Indian Standard Time, stands for:
opts: Navigation with Indian Constellation, India's regional satellite navigation system
questions.why: NavIC covers India and about 1,500 km around it. ISRO's satellites carry atomic clocks.
questions.insight: The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 use NavIC and CSIR-NPL for traceable time.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: India's first hydrogen train was flagged off on 17 July 2026 between Jind and Sonipat (Haryana). It is powered by:
opts: Hydrogen fuel cells, emitting only water vapour
questions.why: A fuel cell combines hydrogen and oxygen to make electricity, with water as the by-product. Jind has a hydrogen facility storing about 3,000 kg.
questions.insight: The route is about 89 km, with an operating speed of 75 km/h.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The National Green Hydrogen Mission, approved in January 2023, aims for a production capacity of:
opts: At least 5 million tonnes of green hydrogen a year by 2030
questions.why: Green hydrogen is made by splitting water with renewable electricity, so it produces no carbon dioxide.
questions.insight: Grey hydrogen comes from natural gas, and blue hydrogen captures its carbon.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The Rs 7,280 crore scheme for sintered Rare Earth Permanent Magnets (REPM) aims to:
opts: Build 6,000 tonnes a year of integrated magnet capacity in India, through five beneficiaries chosen by global bidding
Mine rare earths from the seabed
questions.why: It has sales-linked incentives of Rs 6,450 crore and a capital subsidy of Rs 750 crore. India imports all its sintered NdFeB magnets now.
questions.insight: The Ministry of Heavy Industries extended the bid timeline in July 2026.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: Rare earth permanent magnets (NdFeB) are important mainly because they are used in:
opts: Electric vehicle motors, wind turbines and electronics
questions.why: NdFeB magnets are among the strongest magnets, so they make motors lighter and more efficient.
questions.insight: 'Rare earths' are 17 elements: the 15 lanthanides plus scandium and yttrium.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) number on a mobile phone is:
opts: A 10-digit number identifying the SIM card
The number of the mobile tower
A unique 15-digit number that identifies the handset
questions.why: The Government's Sanchar Saathi portal and the CEIR use the IMEI to block lost or stolen phones. Tampering with IMEIs is prohibited under the 2025 Telecom Cyber Security Rules.
questions.insight: Dialling *#06# usually shows the IMEI.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The BioE3 policy (Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment), approved in 2024, supports biomanufacturing of items such as:
opts: Bio-based chemicals, enzymes and biopolymers such as PLA and PHA
questions.why: The Department of Biotechnology and BIRAC implement it. Parliament was told that projects aim to make PLA and PHA as import substitutes.
questions.insight: Polylactic acid (PLA) is made from plant sugars, for instance from corn or sugarcane, and is biodegradable under industrial composting.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: A plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV) is a vehicle that:
opts: Has both a petrol or diesel engine and a battery that can be charged from an external plug
Runs only on a battery with no engine
questions.why: A PHEV can run for a short distance on its battery and switch to the engine for longer trips.
questions.insight: A battery electric vehicle (BEV) has no engine, and a strong hybrid cannot be plugged in.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: Antifungal resistance is a growing concern. The yeast Candida auris is notable because it:
opts: Resists many antifungal drugs and spreads in hospitals
questions.why: The World Health Organization lists C. auris in its critical priority group of fungal pathogens.
questions.insight: Overuse of antifungals in agriculture and medicine is a driver of resistance.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), for which India is preparing, entered its definitive phase on:
questions.why: The transitional (reporting-only) phase ran from 2023 to 2025. From 2026 importers must account for the carbon embedded in covered goods, with the payment obligation phased in up to 2034.
questions.insight: EU certificate sales for CBAM begin in 2027.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which of the following goods are covered by the EU's CBAM?
opts: Cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen
questions.why: CBAM prices the carbon embedded in carbon-intensive imports to prevent 'carbon leakage'. Importers of more than 50 tonnes of covered goods need authorisation.
questions.insight: India's steel and aluminium exports to the EU are most exposed.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: 'Carbon leakage', the problem CBAM tries to address, means:
opts: Leakage of carbon dioxide from storage tanks
Carbon stored in forests escaping in fires
The loss of carbon credits by accounting error
Industries moving to countries with weaker carbon rules, shifting emissions rather than cutting them
questions.why: If producers move to places with no carbon price, global emissions may not fall. A border tax puts imports on equal terms.
questions.insight: Critics call CBAM a trade barrier and say it conflicts with the principle of 'common but differentiated responsibilities'.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: India's domestic carbon market, the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), is set up under which law?
opts: The Energy Conservation Act, 2001 (as amended in 2022)
questions.why: The Bureau of Energy Efficiency runs the scheme, which sets emission-intensity targets for energy-intensive sectors.
questions.insight: A domestic carbon price may help Indian exporters show they already pay for carbon.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: India launched a Net Zero Portal and an NAPCC Dashboard on World Ozone Day 2026. The National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), launched in 2008, originally had:
opts: Eight national missions, including solar energy, water and sustainable agriculture
Fifty missions, one for each State
questions.why: The original eight missions are solar energy, enhanced energy efficiency, sustainable habitat, water, Himalayan ecosystem, Green India, sustainable agriculture and strategic knowledge.
questions.insight: The dashboard tracks progress of the missions across States and Union Territories.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: World Ozone Day, observed on 16 September, commemorates:
opts: The signing of the Montreal Protocol in 1987
The adoption of the Paris Agreement
questions.why: The Montreal Protocol phases out substances that deplete the ozone layer. The Kigali Amendment (2016) extended it to HFCs, which are powerful greenhouse gases.
questions.insight: India ratified the Kigali Amendment in 2021.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: As per a May 2026 Government update, India's cheetah population under Project Cheetah stood at about:
opts: Zero, as the project has ended
questions.why: Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh is the primary site, and Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary is being prepared as additional habitat. Nine cheetahs arrived from Botswana in February 2026.
questions.insight: The first recorded birth in the wild took place in April 2026.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Project Cheetah reintroduced cheetahs to India from Namibia in September 2022. The cheetah was declared extinct in India in:
questions.why: The Asiatic cheetah vanished from India by the mid-20th century. The animals brought in belong to the African subspecies.
questions.insight: The Asiatic cheetah survives today only in Iran.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Kuno National Park, the main site of Project Cheetah, is located in:
questions.why: The Government plans to widen the project to Gandhi Sagar (Madhya Pradesh), Nauradehi (Madhya Pradesh) and the Banni grasslands (Gujarat).
questions.insight: Grassland and savanna ecosystems need protection, since they are often overlooked.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Which of the following is an area being considered for expanding Project Cheetah beyond Kuno?
opts: The Thar desert dunes of Jaisalmer only
questions.why: A May 2026 Government release names Banni, along with Gandhi Sagar and Nauradehi, as part of the next phase.
questions.insight: Banni is Asia's largest tropical grassland.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Pichavaram, one of India's largest mangrove forests, is in which State?
questions.why: Pichavaram was designated a Ramsar site in 2022, together with Karikili Bird Sanctuary and Pallikaranai Marsh.
questions.insight: The Sundarbans in West Bengal is India's largest mangrove area.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: India's mangrove cover, as per the India State of Forest Report 2023, was about:
opts: 4,992 sq km, about 0.15% of the country's area
questions.why: Mangrove cover rose by about 17 sq km from the 2019 assessment. Mangroves protect coasts and are important nurseries for fish.
questions.insight: The Forest Survey of India, Dehradun, publishes the report every two years.

src.name: PIB, India State of Forest Report 2023

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The MISHTI scheme (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats and Tangible Incomes) aims to:
opts: Restore and plant mangroves along the coast over 2023-24 to 2027-28
questions.why: It targets about 540 sq km in nine coastal States and four Union Territories.
questions.insight: Blue carbon ecosystems such as mangroves store large amounts of carbon.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Copernicus reported that September 2026 was about 1.63°C above the pre-industrial average. The pre-industrial baseline used is:
questions.why: It was the first time since November 2025 that two consecutive months were above 1.5°C. A strong El Niño is adding to the warmth.
questions.insight: The Paris Agreement aims to hold warming well below 2°C and pursue 1.5°C.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The WMO's decadal outlook says there is a high chance that at least one year between 2026 and 2030 will temporarily exceed 1.5°C. This does not by itself mean the Paris goal has failed because:
opts: 1.5°C is measured only in the ocean
Temperatures are measured only in winter
The Paris goal refers to long-term average warming over decades, not a single year
The goal has already been dropped
questions.why: WMO estimates a 91% chance that at least one year in 2026-2030 will exceed 1.5°C above 1850-1900.
questions.insight: The 2024 calendar year was the first to exceed 1.5°C.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Paris Agreement, adopted in 2015, aims to limit global warming to:
opts: Well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels, with efforts to limit it to 1.5°C
questions.why: Countries submit Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) to meet it.
questions.insight: COP31 in Antalya (9 to 20 November 2026) begins the second global stocktake cycle.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: An ICIMOD report in 2026 found that glaciers in the Hindu Kush Himalaya are:
opts: Losing ice at about double the rate since 2000, with some nearing tipping points
questions.why: Glacier area fell about 12% between 1990 and 2020. The report warned that parts of the Himalayan cryosphere may be nearing irreversible retreat.
questions.insight: Melting raises the risk of glacial lake outburst floods.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: ICIMOD's HKH Snow Update 2026 reported that snow persistence in the region was:
opts: About 27.8% below the long-term average, the fourth straight year of decline
questions.why: Snowmelt supplies about a quarter of the region's river water, so repeated shortfalls raise the risk of water shortages.
questions.insight: Consecutive dry years also reduce groundwater and soil moisture.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: ICIMOD, the intergovernmental body that tracks the Hindu Kush Himalaya, has its headquarters in:
questions.why: ICIMOD's eight member countries are Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, Nepal and Pakistan.
questions.insight: The Hindu Kush Himalaya is often called the 'Third Pole' because of its ice.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: World Rhino Day is observed on 22 September. The greater one-horned rhino, found in Assam's Kaziranga, is listed by the IUCN as:
questions.why: Its numbers recovered from about 1,500 in the 1980s to over 4,000, mostly in Assam. Kaziranga had about 2,613 in the 2022 count.
questions.insight: India's other rhino areas include Pobitora (Assam), Jaldapara and Gorumara (West Bengal) and Dudhwa (Uttar Pradesh).

src.name: PIB, Assam's role in protecting rhinos

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: How many of the world's five rhino species are found in India?
questions.why: The five species are the Indian (greater one-horned), Javan, Sumatran, white and black rhinos. Javan rhinos once lived in India but are now only in Indonesia.
questions.insight: India holds the largest population of the greater one-horned rhino; Nepal has the second largest.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) is a principle of the Convention on Biological Diversity under which:
opts: Companies keep all profits from nature
Benefits from using biological resources and traditional knowledge are shared fairly with the countries and communities that provide them
Nations must ban all use of genetic resources
questions.why: The Nagoya Protocol (2010) set out ABS rules. In India, the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 and the National Biodiversity Authority (Chennai) regulate it.
questions.insight: CBD COP17 in Yerevan (19 to 30 October 2026) took up biodiversity decisions.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Green Climate Fund (GCF), whose 46th Board meeting was held on 26 to 29 October 2026, is headquartered in:
questions.why: The GCF was set up under the UNFCCC to channel climate finance to developing countries. In March 2026 its Board approved USD 960.3 million for 18 new projects.
questions.insight: It is the largest dedicated climate fund for developing countries.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: India's National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), whose city ranking Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan was released in September 2026, was launched in:
questions.why: NCAP was launched in January 2019 to cut PM10 and PM2.5 levels in non-attainment cities; the target was later raised to a 40% cut by 2025-26.
questions.insight: 7 September is the International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Himalayan Monal, a colourful pheasant, is the State bird of:
questions.why: It lives in high-altitude forests of the Himalaya and is also called the Impeyan pheasant. Himachal's State bird is the Western tragopan.
questions.insight: Both are Schedule I species under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Kasturirangan Committee (2013) on the Western Ghats recommended that:
opts: About 37% of the Western Ghats (roughly 60,000 sq km) be declared Ecologically Sensitive Area
The whole Western Ghats be opened for mining
questions.why: It was a softened version of the Gadgil Committee (2011), which proposed declaring the entire Ghats as ecologically sensitive.
questions.insight: Six States share the Western Ghats: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

src.name: MoEFCC, Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: The Khair tree (Acacia catechu) is economically important because it yields:
opts: Katha (catechu) used with betel leaf, and hard timber
questions.why: Khair grows in dry deciduous forests and along riverbanks in the sub-Himalayan tract.
questions.insight: Rubber comes from the Hevea tree and quinine from cinchona.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Under India's National Green Hydrogen Mission, which port has been identified as a green hydrogen hub in Gujarat?
questions.why: Kandla, Paradip (Odisha) and Tuticorin (Tamil Nadu) were named as green hydrogen hubs.
questions.insight: Deendayal Port is the old Kandla Port.

src.name: PIB, Three major ports recognised as Green Hydrogen hubs

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q: Permafrost is ground that stays at or below 0°C for:
questions.why: Thawing permafrost releases carbon dioxide and methane, which speeds up warming.
questions.insight: Permafrost is found in the Arctic and in high mountains such as parts of the Himalaya.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Census of India 2027 is being held in two phases. Which is correct?
opts: Houselisting from 1 April to 30 September 2026 (a 30-day window in each State), and population enumeration in February 2027
Population enumeration in 2026 and houselisting in 2028
Both phases in a single week in March 2027
questions.why: The reference date for population enumeration is 00:00 hours on 1 March 2027. Snow-bound areas such as Ladakh were to be counted in September 2026.
questions.insight: Castes will be enumerated in the second phase.

src.name: PIB, Registrar General of India, Census 2027

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: What is new about Census 2027 compared with earlier censuses?
opts: It is the first census to count caste after 1881
It will be run by the Election Commission
It is India's first digital census, with mobile apps and a self-enumeration option
It is held without any field staff
questions.why: More than 30 lakh enumerators and supervisors use a mobile app, and households can self-enumerate for 15 days before the door-to-door visit.
questions.insight: The Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, runs the census.

src.name: PIB, Registrar General of India, Census 2027

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: A 'Census Town' is a settlement that remains administratively rural but is classified as urban for Census purposes. Under the 1981 criteria, it needs:
opts: Population of at least 5,000, at least 75% of male main workers in non-agricultural work, and density of at least 400 per sq km
Population of at least 1 lakh and a municipal corporation
A railway station and a market
questions.why: A 'Statutory Town' has a municipality or similar body by law. A census town does not, though it meets the three criteria.
questions.insight: Many census towns lack urban local bodies, which limits their funds and services.

src.name: Census of India, concepts and definitions

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The National Single Window System (NSWS), which completed five years in September 2026, is run by:
opts: DPIIT, the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
questions.why: It was launched on 22 September 2021 to give investors one portal for Central and State approvals and clearances.
questions.insight: Industrial licence and entrepreneur memorandum processes have moved fully onto NSWS.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: From 1 October 2026, domestic LPG consumers must complete Biometric Aadhaar Authentication to book refills at the subsidised rate. Those who do not:
opts: Can still buy LPG, but at the market price without subsidy
questions.why: On 19 September 2026, 27.43 crore consumers (89.9%) had already completed it. Options include the delivery visit, the distributor's showroom and OMC apps.
questions.insight: LPG subsidy is paid by Direct Benefit Transfer under the PAHAL scheme.

src.name: PIB, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Aadhaar-based biometric authentication for government benefits is backed by which law?
opts: The National Food Security Act, 2013 only
The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016
questions.why: Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act allows Aadhaar to be required for subsidies and benefits funded from the Consolidated Fund of India.
questions.insight: In the Puttaswamy case (2018) the Supreme Court upheld Aadhaar for welfare but limited its use for private services.

src.name: PIB, Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The DDU-GKY 2.0 guidelines of the Ministry of Rural Development, notified in 2025, set which key rule?
opts: A minimum placement period of six months (up from three), with 12 months of post-placement tracking
A fixed salary of Rs 50,000 for all trainees
questions.why: The scheme targets rural youth aged 15 to 35 and keeps a minimum 576-hour training course. The Budget 2026-27 gave it Rs 750 crore.
questions.insight: DDU-GKY began in 2014 and is observed on Antyodaya Diwas.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Ayurveda Day is now observed on a fixed date each year, which is:
questions.why: The Government fixed 23 September (around the autumnal equinox) as the permanent date, replacing Dhanteras and Dhanwantari Jayanti. The Ministry of Ayush leads the day.
questions.insight: The first Ayurveda Day was observed in 2016.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Attorney General for India, appointed under Article 76, is a person who:
opts: Is qualified to be a Supreme Court judge and holds office during the pleasure of the President
Is elected by Parliament for five years
Must be a sitting High Court judge
questions.why: The Attorney General is the Government's chief legal adviser and has the right to speak in Parliament (Article 88) but cannot vote.
questions.insight: The Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General assist the Attorney General.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office:
opts: By the Chief Justice of India alone
By a simple majority in the Lok Sabha
In the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge (Article 324(5))
questions.why: Removal needs a special majority in both Houses on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. Other Election Commissioners can be removed only on the CEC's recommendation.
questions.insight: This protects the Commission's independence.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Under the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, appointments are recommended by a committee of:
opts: The Prime Minister and the Home Minister only
The Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM, and the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha
The Chief Justice of India, the Prime Minister and the President
The Speaker, the Vice-President and the Chief Justice
questions.why: The 2023 Act replaced the Chief Justice of India, who the Supreme Court had put on the panel in 2023, with a Union Cabinet Minister.
questions.insight: The President appoints on the committee's recommendation.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Under Article 124(3), which of the following can be appointed a Supreme Court judge?
opts: Only a sitting High Court Chief Justice
A distinguished jurist in the President's opinion, among other categories
questions.why: The other categories are a judge of a High Court for at least five years and an advocate of a High Court for at least ten years.
questions.insight: Appointments follow the Collegium system laid down in the Second and Third Judges cases.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The 99th Constitutional Amendment (2014), which created the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC), was:
opts: Repealed by the Rajya Sabha alone
Struck down by the Supreme Court in 2015, restoring the Collegium system
Upheld, and the NJAC now works
questions.why: In the Fourth Judges Case (2015) the Court held the NJAC violated judicial independence, a part of the basic structure.
questions.insight: The Collegium for the Supreme Court includes the CJI and four senior-most judges.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, an Internal Committee must be set up where there are:
opts: No threshold; a court handles all complaints
10 or more employees; smaller workplaces use a Local Committee at the district level
questions.why: The Act gives statutory form to the Vishaka Guidelines (1997).
questions.insight: The Vishaka case is Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Article 22(1) of the Constitution gives a person who is arrested the right to:
opts: Be informed of the grounds of arrest and to consult a lawyer of their choice
Remain silent only before a magistrate
questions.why: Article 22(2) also requires the person to be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours. The Supreme Court has held that the grounds should be given in writing in a language the person understands.
questions.insight: Article 22 also lays down safeguards for preventive detention, with an Advisory Board for detention beyond three months.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: In the 2002 case Indian National Congress (I) v. Institute of Social Welfare, the Supreme Court held that the Election Commission:
opts: Can ban a party for one election at will
Has no general power to deregister a political party, except in cases such as fraud or a party being declared unlawful
Can deregister any party that loses elections
questions.why: This is why inactive Registered Unrecognised Political Parties can only be delisted in limited cases, and reforms such as deregistration after ten years without contesting have been proposed.
questions.insight: The ECI registers parties under Section 29A of the RP Act, 1951.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Under the Forest Rights Act, 2006, the authority to initiate the process of determining and verifying forest rights is the:
questions.why: The Act recognises individual and community rights, including minor forest produce, and its nodal ministry is the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
questions.insight: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 was renamed the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam in 2023.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Article 243A of the Constitution says the Gram Sabha:
opts: Has no role in a Panchayat
May exercise powers and perform functions at the village level as the State legislature decides
Is a court of law at the village level
questions.why: Part IX, added by the 73rd Amendment (1992), makes the Gram Sabha the base of the three-tier Panchayati Raj system.
questions.insight: The Panchayati Raj Ministry's Gram Panchayat Development Plans are approved in the Gram Sabha.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) merged which earlier schemes for Scheduled Castes?
opts: Pradhan Mantri Adarsh Gram Yojana, Special Central Assistance to the SC Sub-Plan, and Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana
questions.why: The merged scheme, from 2021-22, covers SC-majority village development, income schemes and hostels.
questions.insight: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment runs it.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act, 1958 (AFSPA) can be applied in an area only after it is declared:
opts: A 'disturbed area' by the Central Government or the Governor of the State
questions.why: Section 3 allows the declaration, and the Act gives the armed forces special powers such as arrest without warrant and use of force.
questions.insight: AFSPA has been withdrawn from several areas, such as Tripura (2015) and Meghalaya (2018).

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: COBRA (Commando Battalion for Resolute Action) is a specialised unit of which force?
opts: CRPF, raised to fight Left-Wing Extremism
questions.why: COBRA battalions were set up in 2008-09 for jungle warfare against Maoists.
questions.insight: Left-Wing Extremism is concentrated in the 'Red Corridor'.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Jhiram Ghati attack, in which Maoists killed 27 people including Congress leaders in Bastar, took place on:
questions.why: The ambush hit a convoy returning from a 'Parivartan Rally' on 25 May 2013.
questions.insight: The NIA, set up under the NIA Act, 2008 after 26/11, investigated the attack.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: The Defence Minister released the 'RAKSHA' document on 3 September 2026. It is:
opts: A ten-year roadmap for India's defence diplomacy and global defence partnerships
A list of new fighter jets
questions.why: Its pillars are strategic partnerships, capacity building through exercises and training, defence exports under Make in India, and a larger maritime role as a net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region.
questions.insight: It complements the MAHASAGAR vision, which stands for Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: In May 2026, India and Vietnam raised their relationship to which level?
questions.why: Vietnam's General Secretary and President To Lam visited India from 5 to 7 May 2026. Outcomes included an IREL rare earths MoU and an RBI–State Bank of Vietnam payments MoU.
questions.insight: Vietnam is a key partner in India's Act East Policy and Indo-Pacific vision.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The India–EU Free Trade Agreement, whose negotiations were concluded on 27 January 2026, gives Indian exporters:
opts: Preferential access for over 99% of exports by trade value to the EU
questions.why: The EU also made commitments across 144 services subsectors. India protected sensitive sectors such as dairy, cereals and poultry.
questions.insight: Negotiations were relaunched in 2022 after a pause since 2013.

src.name: PIB, Ministry of Commerce, India-EU FTA

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: On 14 September 2026, India and MERCOSUR launched negotiations to:
opts: Set up a joint space agency
Expand their existing Preferential Trade Agreement
questions.why: MERCOSUR's pro tempore president for the period was Uruguay. The Terms of Reference were being finalised.
questions.insight: MERCOSUR's full members are Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay (Venezuela is suspended; Bolivia is acceding).

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: Which of these is NOT a full member of MERCOSUR?
questions.why: Chile is an associate state, not a full member.
questions.insight: MERCOSUR was founded by the Treaty of Asunción (1991).

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: Which statement about the SCO is correct?
opts: Its headquarters is in New Delhi
It has no mutual security focus
India became a full member in 2017 along with Pakistan
questions.why: The SCO secretariat is in Beijing and its Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) is in Tashkent. The 26th summit was in Bishkek on 31 August–1 September 2026.
questions.insight: Founding members were China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and (from 2001) Uzbekistan.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The BRICS grouping, whose 18th summit was held on 12–13 September 2026, originally took shape with which countries?
opts: Brazil, Russia, India, China and Iran
