Brazil, Russia, India and China (South Africa joined in 2010)
questions.why: 'BRIC' was coined by economist Jim O'Neill in 2001. The first leaders' summit was in 2009.
questions.insight: India chaired BRICS in 2026.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS, 1982) gives a coastal state an Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of up to:
questions.why: The territorial sea is 12 nm, the contiguous zone 24 nm. The continental shelf can extend to 350 nm under conditions.
questions.insight: India ratified UNCLOS in 1995.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The principle of 'innocent passage' under UNCLOS applies in which maritime zone?
questions.why: Foreign ships may pass through the territorial sea if they do not harm the peace, order or security of the coastal state.
questions.insight: Ships have the freedom of navigation in the EEZ and on the high seas.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The Indus Waters Treaty (1960) was signed between India and Pakistan with the mediation of:
questions.why: The treaty gives India the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) and Pakistan the three western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab), with limited Indian use of the western rivers.
questions.insight: A Court of Arbitration issued an award in August 2026 on the treaty's provisions.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: India and the US co-develop and co-produce defence items such as the Javelin anti-tank missile under which initiative?
questions.why: DTTI was launched in 2012 to co-produce and co-develop defence items.
questions.insight: COMCASA, LEMOA, BECA and GSOMIA are India–US foundational agreements; India has signed the first three.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The Quad groups India with which three countries?
questions.why: It focuses on a free and open Indo-Pacific, with working groups on health, technology and maritime domain awareness.
questions.insight: AUKUS is a different arrangement: Australia, UK and US.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: India's current account deficit in Q1 2026-27 was:
questions.why: The merchandise trade deficit was around US$86 billion, but remittances (US$42.9 billion) and services receipts kept the gap small.
questions.insight: India is the world's largest recipient of remittances.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Gross GST collections in April–September 2026 were about:
opts: Rs 12.46 lakh crore, up 11.6% year on year
questions.why: Registered GST taxpayers reached about 1.70 crore, up from around 60 lakh in 2017.
questions.insight: GST has been in force since 1 July 2017 under the 101st Constitutional Amendment.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The GST Council is a constitutional body under which Article?
questions.why: It is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, and the Centre has one-third of the voting weight and States two-thirds. Decisions need three-fourths of the weighted votes.
questions.insight: Article 246A gives both Parliament and State legislatures the power to make GST laws.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has how many members, and who has the casting vote?
opts: Six; the RBI Governor has a casting vote in case of a tie
questions.why: Three members are from the RBI and three are external members appointed by the Government.
questions.insight: The MPC targets CPI inflation of 4% with a tolerance band of plus or minus 2%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: In June 2026 the MPC kept the repo rate at 5.25%. Which one tool changes the rate at which banks borrow from the RBI against government securities?
opts: The bank rate for term loans
questions.why: The standing deposit facility (SDF) rate sits 25 basis points below the repo and the MSF rate 25 basis points above it.
questions.insight: The RBI raised the repo rate to 5.50% in October 2026.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 as amended, the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) requires banks to hold:
opts: A share of their deposits in liquid assets such as government securities, gold and cash
A share of deposits with the RBI in cash only
questions.why: CRR is held with the RBI; SLR is held by the banks themselves.
questions.insight: The statutory SLR ceiling is 40% of net demand and time liabilities.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999 replaced:
questions.why: FEMA made foreign exchange violations civil rather than criminal matters. The RBI and the Directorate of Enforcement play key roles.
questions.insight: FEMA is administered by the Ministry of Finance.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003 seeks to:
opts: Bring in fiscal discipline by setting targets for the fiscal deficit and debt
questions.why: The N.K. Singh Committee (2017) recommended a debt-to-GDP target of 60% for the General Government, with the Centre at 40%.
questions.insight: Escape clauses allow deviations for reasons such as war, national calamity or severe slowdown.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Minimum Support Price (MSP) is recommended by:
opts: The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)
questions.why: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approves it. The CACP recommends MSP for 22 mandated crops and Fair and Remunerative Price for sugarcane.
questions.insight: FCI procures foodgrains at MSP for the buffer stock.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The 81st session of the UN General Assembly (September 2026) has the theme:
opts: Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations that Delivers for All
questions.why: Its General Debate in late September was where India's External Affairs Minister spoke on reform of the international order.
questions.insight: The UNGA has 193 member states, each with one vote.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: At the UN, the G4 group that pushes for Security Council reform consists of:
questions.why: The G4 seek permanent seats for each other. The Uniting for Consensus group, led by Italy and Pakistan, opposes new permanent seats.
questions.insight: India says new permanent members must hold the same rights, including the veto, as the existing ones.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: Which of these is NOT a permanent member of the UN Security Council?
questions.why: The five permanent members (P5) are China, France, Russia, the UK and the US. There are also ten elected non-permanent members serving two-year terms.
questions.insight: A veto by any P5 member blocks a substantive resolution.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: Non-permanent members of the UN Security Council are elected by the General Assembly for a term of:
questions.why: Five are elected each year, and a retiring member cannot be re-elected immediately.
questions.insight: India served its eighth term in 2021-22.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) has its seat in:
questions.why: It is the principal judicial organ of the UN and has 15 judges elected for nine-year terms.
questions.insight: The International Criminal Court, also in The Hague, is not a UN organ.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is in:
questions.why: The IAEA verifies that nuclear material is used peacefully and administers safeguards.
questions.insight: The Nuclear Suppliers Group, which India has been seeking to join, decides on export of nuclear materials.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The Gulf of Mannar and Palk Strait separate India from:
questions.why: Adam's Bridge (Ram Setu) lies between Rameswaram and Mannar. Katchatheevu island lies in the Palk Strait.
questions.insight: The 1974 and 1976 agreements fixed the maritime boundary between India and Sri Lanka.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project connects India with:
questions.why: It links Kolkata to Sittwe port in Myanmar and then to Mizoram by river and road, giving the Northeast another route.
questions.insight: The India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway is a separate project.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The Durand Line is the boundary between:
questions.why: It was drawn in 1893 between British India and Afghanistan. Afghanistan has not recognised it as an international border.
questions.insight: The McMahon Line concerns India and China, and the Radcliffe Line India and Pakistan.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: Which Indian State does NOT share a border with Bangladesh?
questions.why: The States bordering Bangladesh are West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
questions.insight: India–Bangladesh land boundary was settled by the 2015 Land Boundary Agreement.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The Pravasi Bharatiya Divas is celebrated every year on:
questions.why: It marks Mahatma Gandhi's return to India from South Africa in 1915.
questions.insight: It is observed by the Ministry of External Affairs.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) has how many members?
opts: Eleven, after Timor-Leste joined in October 2025
questions.why: Timor-Leste became the 11th member in 2025. The ASEAN Secretariat is in Jakarta.
questions.insight: India's Act East Policy is built on ASEAN centrality.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: India's Consumer Price Index now uses base year 2024=100. Combined retail inflation for August 2026 was:
questions.why: Food inflation on the Consumer Food Price Index was 5.95%. Onion inflation jumped to about 48%, while tomato prices fell by about 31%.
questions.insight: The RBI's inflation target is 4% with a band of 2% to 6%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Consumer Price Index is compiled and released by:
opts: The National Statistical Office under MoSPI
questions.why: The Wholesale Price Index, by contrast, is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
questions.insight: The RBI uses CPI (Combined) for its inflation target.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: India's real GDP growth in Q1 of 2026-27 (April–June 2026) was estimated at:
questions.why: The National Statistics Office released the figure on 1 September 2026. GDP is measured at constant (2011-12) prices unless a new base is announced.
questions.insight: Gross Value Added differs from GDP by net product taxes.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, the Committee of Creditors needs what share of votes to approve a resolution plan?
questions.why: The 2019 amendment lowered the threshold from 75% to 66%. The National Company Law Tribunal is the adjudicating authority for companies.
questions.insight: The IBBI regulates insolvency professionals.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: SEBI, the securities market regulator, was given statutory powers by:
questions.why: SEBI was set up administratively in 1988 and became a statutory body in 1992.
questions.insight: The Securities Appellate Tribunal hears appeals against SEBI orders.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body under which Article, and how often is it constituted?
questions.why: It recommends the share of States in central taxes. The 16th Finance Commission, headed by Arvind Panagariya, reports for 2026-27 to 2030-31.
questions.insight: Its recommendations are advisory, not binding.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Priority sector lending by banks includes loans to:
opts: Agriculture, MSMEs, education, housing and weaker sections
questions.why: The overall target is 40% of adjusted net bank credit for domestic banks.
questions.insight: Small finance banks have a higher target of 75%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) is operated by:
opts: The Ministry of Electronics and IT
The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)
questions.why: NPCI is an umbrella organisation for retail payments set up by the RBI and the Indian Banks' Association. It also runs RuPay.
questions.insight: The RBI regulates payment systems under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The 'Kisan Credit Card' scheme provides farmers with:
opts: Short-term credit for crops and allied activities at concessional interest
questions.why: The Interest Subvention Scheme reduces the effective interest rate for timely repayment.
questions.insight: NABARD refinances rural credit.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The World Trade Organization (WTO) replaced the GATT in:
questions.why: WTO is headquartered in Geneva. Its Ministerial Conference is the highest decision-making body and meets at least every two years.
questions.insight: The WTO dispute settlement body's Appellate Body has been non-functional since 2019.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Which of the following is a capital receipt in the Union Budget?
questions.why: Capital receipts create a liability or reduce an asset: borrowings, loan recoveries and disinvestment.
questions.insight: The fiscal deficit equals total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation's Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) is based in:
questions.why: The SCO secretariat is in Beijing, while RATS works from Tashkent.
questions.insight: India joined the SCO as a full member in 2017.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were set up under the Regional Rural Banks Act of:
questions.why: They are owned jointly by the Centre (50%), the sponsor bank (35%) and the State (15%).
questions.insight: The Narasimham Working Group recommended them in 1975.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: Zero-Based Budgeting means:
opts: Every expense must be justified afresh each cycle, not carried over from the past
A budget with no expenditure on defence
questions.why: It contrasts with incremental budgeting, which adds to the previous year's base.
questions.insight: Outcome budgeting links spending to measurable results.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of these is a west-flowing river that drains into the Arabian Sea?
questions.why: Narmada and Tapi flow west through rift valleys. Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi flow east to the Bay of Bengal.
questions.insight: The Narmada originates at Amarkantak.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The 'Loo' is:
opts: A hot, dry summer wind over the northern plains
A cold wave from the Himalayas
questions.why: It blows in May-June in the afternoon from the Thar side.
questions.insight: Western disturbances bring winter rain to the north-west.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Western Ghats are known officially as:
opts: Sahyadri, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2012
questions.why: Anamudi (2,695 m) in Kerala is the highest peak in the range.
questions.insight: The Eastern Ghats are older and more broken.

questions.subject: Geography
